c.tagline: Sun-bleached Indian Ocean capital of Afro-Latin rhythm and colonial grandeur.

taxi.color: white with a colored stripe (often blue/green)
taxi.fareNote: Most taxis lack working meters; agree the fare in cash before departing, or use a rideshare app like Yango where available.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; many visitors call hotel/embassy contacts or private medical services (e.g. Clinica Cruz Azul) directly for serious issues.

hood_landmark.Costa do Sol: Costa do Sol Restaurant, Avenida Marginal, Maputo

avoid.reason: Petty crime and bag-snatching; caution at night; police shakedowns — carry ID copies

hood_desc: Polana (Cimento), the leafy, embassy-lined heart of the city with tree-shaded avenues, upscale hotels and restaurants; best for first-time visitors wanting comfort and easy walking to sights.
Sommerschield, a quiet residential and diplomatic quarter next to Polana with guesthouses and boutique stays; suits business travelers and those wanting a calmer base near embassies.

Baixa (city centre/downtown), the historic colonial core near the port and train station with markets, museums and budget-to-midrange lodging; suits travelers who want to walk to landmarks and nightlife.
Costa do Sol, the breezy Marginal beachfront strip northeast of downtown known for seafood restaurants and sea views; suits travelers who want a relaxed, scenic base near the water.
Malhangalene, a mixed local residential and commercial neighborhood with more affordable guesthouses; suits budget travelers wanting an authentic, less touristy feel close to the center.
lodging: Costa do Sol Hotel and Restaurant

water.note: Tap water is not recommended for visitors; use bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: Bus and chapa fares are paid in cash (small metical notes/coins) directly to the driver or conductor on board; there is no citywide contactless fare card. Have exact change ready, as chapas are informal and crowded.
transit.hours: Buses and chapas run roughly 5:00-21:00; service thins out after dark and few options run late night, so taxis or rideshare are recommended after dusk.
transit.note: Public transport is crowded, informal and best suited to confident travelers; most visitors rely on taxis, hotel transfers, or the Yango app for convenience and safety.

train: CFM commuter rail to Machava/Matola (limited tourist use)
Sitting service toward Ressano Garcia (South Africa border)
bus: Intercape/long-distance coaches to Johannesburg and regional cities
ferry: Small passenger boats/dhows across Maputo Bay to Catembe (largely superseded by the Maputo-Katembe Bridge)

tip.r: Not obligatory but appreciated; round up taxi fares and leave ~10% at sit-down restaurants where a service charge isn't already included.
